title: Lease-anchored slot reclamation with skyline-watermark invariants for prefix-coherent KV cache
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's KV cache is critical for continuous batching performance. Current hybrid LRU/TTL strategies reduce miss rates but leave edge cases where prefix-affinity (multiple in-flight requests sharing prefixes) and lease/TTL interactions can cause either premature eviction or memory holds that prevent batch throughput. This ticket designs and implements a lease-anchored slot reclamation mechanism with a skyline-watermark invariant to ensure prefix-consistent correctness and bounded staleness while improving GPU memory compaction.

Goals:
- Introduce a slot-based reclamation layer on top of existing KV slabs that: (1) groups entries into short-lived "slots" aligned with live leases; (2) allows bulk reclamation when skyline watermarks indicate safe compacting without violating prefix-affinity constraints.
- Define formal invariants that guarantee no request will observe a missing prefix entry if the request's lease claims it should be visible (prefix linearizability relative to lease epochs).
- Ensure eviction decisions respect a hybrid score combining LRU recency, TTL expiration, and prefix-affinity weight, but underpinned by the skyline-watermark safety check to avoid unsafe reclamation during concurrent prefetch/evict cycles.
- Reduce long-tail GPU memory spikes by 20% on 95th percentile and maintain token-latency SLOs (p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms) for typical production workloads.

Design overview (high level):
1) Slots and leases:
   - Each cache shard maintains a circular sequence of slots (configurable length N, default 128).
   - Each entry is pinned to a slot when created or prefetched; slot assignment is based on the active lease epoch of the request that populated it.
   - Leases have short lifetimes aligned to batching windows (e.g., 50-200ms) to provide coalescing semantics for continuous batching.

2) Skyline-watermark invariant:
   - Maintain two monotonic watermarks per shard: reclaimable_watermark and safe_visibility_watermark.
   - reclaimable_watermark <= safe_visibility_watermark always. reclaimable_watermark marks the latest slot index eligible for reclamation by default; safe_visibility_watermark marks the latest slot index whose entries are guaranteed visible to any in-flight request with an earlier lease epoch.
   - Reclamation can only free slots with index <= reclaimable_watermark AND only when safe_visibility_watermark has advanced beyond them.

3) Hybrid scoring and prefix-affinity:
   - Each entry has a score = alpha*recency_rank + beta*(TTL_expiry_score) + gamma*(prefix_affinity_score). Coeffs tunable via runtime config.
   - Prefix affinity scoring increases weight for entries observed in multi-request prefix cohorts. This biases retention for hot prefixes even if recency is lower, but the skyline invariant prevents this from producing inconsistent visibility.

4) Correctness invariants (to prove/validate):
   - V1 (No-unsafe-evict): A slot can be reclaimed only if all in-flight leases that could reference its prefixes have ended or the safe_visibility_watermark has advanced.
   - V2 (Prefix-linearizability): For any prefix P and times t1 < t2, if a request at t2 observes value v for P, then any request at t1 that had a lease intersecting t2 must not observe a value that implies v was already evicted inconsistent with lease semantics.
   - V3 (Bounded-staleness): The maximum time between an entry's logical expiration (TTL or explicit invalidation) and physical reclamation is bounded by R ms (configurable default 500ms).

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (design + testing harness): author a standalone simulation harness (python + property-based tests using Hypothesis) to encode skyline-watermark transitions and validate invariants under adversarial lease and prefetch patterns. Link: docs/design/slot-reclaim-harness.md.
- Phase B (shard-level runtime): implement slot metadata (compact u32 slot index per entry) and skyline watermarks; add reclamation worker loop with feature-flag. Ensure memory layout keeps entry footprint minimal (<= 8 bytes overhead).
- Phase C (scoring + telemetry): plug hybrid scoring into eviction path, add per-prefix counters, expose metrics (slot_free_rate, skyline_lag_ms, bad-evict-events).
- Phase D (canary rollout): behind a rollout flag, enable on dedicated staging GPU cluster and run A/B experiments vs baseline eviction with synthetic prefix-heavy workloads and production trace replay.

Acceptance criteria:
- Property-based harness shows zero invariant violations across 10k random lease/prefetch scenarios and targeted adversarial traces.
- Unit + integration tests added covering: reclaimable_watermark advancement, safe_visibility gating, score-driven eviction decisions, and eviction under heavy prefetch bursts.
- Benchmarks: 95th-percentile GPU memory usage reduced by >= 15% (goal 20%), end-to-end token latency p95 unchanged or improved by <= +5% relative delta.
- No observed production regressions in canary; rollout to 25% of dedicated capacity with rollback instrumentation ready.

Key tradeoffs and decisions considered:
- Option A: aggressive slot trimming yields lower memory but higher coordination; Option B: conservative TTL-based reclaiming simpler but leaves fragmentation. We pick hybrid slot-level reclaiming gated by skyline-watermark to get best of both while keeping correctness checks lightweight.
- We prefer lease epochs aligned to batching windows (short leases) rather than per-request unique ids to limit metadata churn. This increases chance of coalescing but requires careful watermark progression.

Testing strategy and coverage:
- Property tests: use hypothes.is-like fuzz harness to verify invariants under randomized lease durations, out-of-order request completion, and simulated crashes.
- Fuzz harness in CI that runs 1M operations nightly (fast mode for PRs ~50k ops).
- Integration: run production trace replay for 12 hours on staging with feature-flag on and compare cache hit/miss, evict anomalies, and skyline lag.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Feature flag rollout plan: off -> 10% canary (dedicated staging) -> 25% (limited prod) -> 100% (release).
- Critical metrics to watch: slot_free_rate, skyline_lag_ms, eviction_conflicts (counter for attempted reclaim blocked by safe_visibility), prefix_miss_regressions, p95_memory. Alert if eviction_conflicts spike or prefix_miss_regressions > 0.5% relative.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should slot size be adaptive per-shard based on observed prefix cohort cardinality? (defer to follow-up ticket if needed)
- Interaction with long-lived private deployments: consider exposing per-customer TTL/lease knobs.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: docs/design/slot-reclaim-harness.md
- Simulation harness: repo/tools/kv_slot_harness/README.md
- Draft RFC: docs/rfc/2026-02-slot-reclaim-rfc.md

Implementation notes:
- Keep on-disk/host-visible metadata minimal: single 32-bit slot index + 16-bit affinity score saturating counter per entry.
- Reclamation worker must use a fast path: check reclaimable_watermark and safe_visibility_watermark stamp without acquiring per-entry locks; only in contested cases acquire per-prefix fence.
